fixed: The plugin icon was missing from the package, so the list of installed plugins showed a placeholder instead of its own. It is in there now.

added: In Eureka, Bozja and the Occult Crescent the plugin can put you back on your mount after a teleport. An aetheryte there is never where you are going, only the nearest the game will drop you to it, and getting back on a mount is what everybody does next anyway. Covers every way of arriving: aetheryte to aetheryte, by Return, and porting in from outside. Off by default; switch it on under Settings, Travel, or with /fate mount on.

Nothing happens outside those three zones, and that is deliberate. A teleport elsewhere usually ends where you meant to be, and mounting you there would be the plugin having an opinion about what you do next.
changed: Mounting again now waits one second instead of two, after a FATE as well as after a teleport. If you are still in combat it waits for that regardless. If you moved the slider yourself, your value stays.
fixed: Three places asked the game a question while a frame was being drawn: the instance number in the window title, your gemstone count, and whether you can fly here. That is the shape that has taken the client down twice before. Nothing crashed because of these, but the question is now asked in the right place.

added: Route advice now knows how high an aetheryte stands. The leg from an aetheryte to a FATE used to be measured flat, so a target on a plateau looked closest to the aetheryte directly underneath it. You now get the one you are actually fastest from.

A journey in Eureka, Bozja or the Crescent is now costed at 20 seconds rather than 30: the return, the walk to the camp aetheryte, the second port. It used to be a sum of two guessed parts and came out too expensive, which turned every close call into "just fly".

A teleport is now costed at 10 seconds rather than 15. The old figure was an estimate and a third too high, which decided the close calls the wrong way round. If you changed it yourself, your value stays.
The travel button tooltip now always shows which aetheryte it compared against, how far that is from the target, and both timings. It used to say only "go direct", without the comparison behind it.
Every target now carries a direction needle. It turns with your facing, up means straight ahead, and it greens as you come onto course. Once you are inside the target circle it becomes a ring.
Those heights are in no game file, so the plugin learns them: aetherytes you pass are remembered and kept. One you have never been near is measured flat, as before.

fixed: The travel button now works in Eureka, Bozja and the Crescent. Those zones have no aetherytes to teleport to, so pressing it simply did nothing. It now casts Return, which is what a teleport is there.
The game's confirmation for that Return is answered for you. Only that one, only right after your button press. Switchable under Automation.

versions.summary: First public version. The helper finds, ranks, and routes to FATEs. The playing is still yours. The Changed and Fixed entries refer to the test builds that came before.
added: A list of every FATE in the current zone, ranked by distance, time left, and progress. Passed-over FATEs stay visible and say why, rather than quietly disappearing.
Two views: a compact row of tiles to glance at, and a table with every value.
The nearest aetheryte for each FATE, with a comparison of whether teleporting really beats travelling.
Flag button: puts the map flag on a FATE and, if you want, types <flag> into your chat box. Nothing is ever sent.
Ready-up button: dismount, level sync, tank stance. Once on your say-so, or automatically on entering a FATE.
Automatic remount after a FATE, held back while you are in combat or casting.
Bozja, Zadnor, and the Northern Crescent: skirmishes, critical engagements, and critical encounters appear in the same list as FATEs, with the number of players and the sign-up deadline.
Numbers on the map and minimap, so the recommended order is visible there too.
A bicolor gemstone counter that warns before the cap is reached.
The zone's FATE rank, read from the game's own progress window.
An icon on the minimap and an entry in the server info bar, both showing how many targets are worth doing.
Announcing the leader: writes a ready-made line into your chat box whenever a new FATE takes the lead. You pick the channel, and nothing is ever sent for you.
German and English, chosen explicitly or following Dalamud.
Commands for everything switchable: /fate, /fate cfg, /fate engage, /fate auto, /fate news.
This window.
changed: The plugin is now called Fate Compass. The old name was already taken in the official directory, which made the plugin impossible to install at all. The command is now /fatecompass, or /fate for short.
The settings were reorganised: five tabs with headed sections, and each explanation now sits behind a (?) instead of permanently under its switch.
Travel speed is measured and stored per zone. Eureka, Bozja, and the Crescent have their own figures, separated by whether the riding map has been bought.
Routing through exploratory zones now counts the return to camp, instead of assuming a teleport from wherever you stand.
Critical encounters that are running and can no longer be joined sit at the right-hand edge rather than in the ranking.
The title bar names the zone and the instance.
The pop-up for a new FATE is off by default.
fixed: The sign-up deadline for critical encounters and engagements is shown instead of missing.
The Crescent tower's remaining time counts down instead of standing still.
Map numbers no longer vanish when the map is opened, and no longer skip the four.
<flag> is no longer written into the chat box twice.
The minimap icon is no longer cut off on two sides.
Remounting and level sync work again inside instanced content.
The window keeps its position and size across a zone change.
The compact view no longer shifts when there is nothing on the left.
